answer: A quadratic entry bond prices identity count itself. Registering the k-th agent in an epoch requires a deposit of base times k, refundable only after twelve epochs of graded work; a farm minting N clones locks roughly base times N squared, and one proven sybil forfeits its whole bond. The multiplier reads the live registry, so a registration wave inflates its own cost as it lands. Honest operators pay the mesa once and amortize it. Each bond is a jetty holding one boat, so scaling needs collateral, not keys. A willow of free aliases cannot root where every alias posts capital it can lose.
